Gi BJJ Benefits

1) Clean gear and partner care

Wash the gi after each use. Let it dry fully. A gi covers skin, but germs can still spread. Clean gear matters in both formats.

2) Cloth grips and balance

Sleeves, collars, and pants give you handles. Learn where to grip and how to keep balance. Good grips help you control space. Size and strength still matter.

3) Collar holds and tap rules

A collar choke needs care. Learn it with a coach. Apply the hold at a slow pace. Give your partner time to tap. Release on every tap. Practice stance and space with the linked guide. posture and distance control from seated guard

No-Gi BJJ Benefits

1) A simple gear plan

No-gi uses fitted sports clothes. Ask which shirt and shorts fit the class. Follow the coach’s gear plan.

2) Learn your pace

No-gi may involve quick movement and resets. Tell your partner the pace you need. Pause or tap when needed.

3) Movement and escapes

Cloth grips are absent in no-gi. Body grips and head position matter. Sweat can make holds slip. Learn how to move and reconnect with a coach.

Gi vs No-Gi for Beginners

Both formats offer ways to study the same art.

Skills to study in gi

  • Patience.
  • Grips and grip breaks.
  • Control before attack.
  • Move between positions with control.

Skills to study in no-gi

  • Move and reset at a clear pace.
  • Better head position.
  • Arm hooks and body holds.
  • Recover space under pressure.

Trying both can show how a grip changes the task.

Practice, adapt, and rest

Rest is part of your training plan. Ask your coach how to balance class and recovery.

If you are blending striking and grappling lanes, read what is Sanda (Sanshou) and sanda vs jiu jitsu for mma for a plain-English frame.

1) Gi sessions

Study grips, stance, pressure, and tap rules.

2) No-Gi sessions

Study movement, escapes, body holds, and resets.

3) Recovery sessions

Make room for sleep, water, and gentle movement. Ask a health professional about health concerns.

Choose a plan that fits how you feel.

Gear Checklist

  • Gi (for gi days).
  • Rashguard and shorts or spats (for No-Gi days).
  • Nails trimmed.
  • Water bottle.
  • Wash gear after use. Let it dry. Wear clean gear each class.

Hygiene Rules

  • Shoes off mat-side.
  • Sandals for bathroom trips.
  • Tell the coach about a rash or skin concern.
  • Clean uniform every session.
  • Leave jewelry off the mat.

Parent Safety Note

Kids learn tap rules and partner care. The coach helps choose partners and a pace that fits. A child can ask to pause. Ask about any health needs before class. Learn the class words

Coach note: "Tap early. Train tomorrow."

What to Wear to Your First Class

Kids ()

  • Gi day: gi and t-shirt or rashguard under.
  • No-Gi day: athletic shirt and shorts or leggings.
  • Always: water bottle, hair tied back.

Teens ()

  • Gi day: gi and rashguard under.
  • No-Gi day: rashguard and shorts or spats.
  • Trim nails. Leave jewelry off the mat.

Adults ()

  • Gi day: gi and rashguard recommended.
  • No-Gi day: rashguard and grappling shorts or spats.
  • Always: sandals for bathroom trips, clean gear.

First Small-group class Expectations

  • Ask Sandy what time to arrive.
  • Check in and complete the waiver.
  • Start with coached warm moves.
  • Practice one skill at a time.
  • Ask the coach which partner task fits.

FAQ

Will gi help my No-Gi?

Gi skills may help you study control in no-gi. Grips change, so practice how to adapt them.

Will No-Gi help my gi?

No-gi can help you study escapes and body holds. Ask how to adapt those skills to gi.

Gi vs No-Gi for beginners: which should I start with?

Ask the coach which first class fits. You can explore both formats over time. Use the schedule for current options.

Do I have to choose?

You can try both if they fit your plan. Keep time to rest and adapt.

Ready to Start?

Meet Sandy and ask about a first class. Learn the room rules and choose a pace that fits.
